title: mexxi configuration
description: Everything a mexxi user may set differently, read from ~/.config/mexxi/config.json (or MEXXI_CONFIG). Every key is optional; an unset key takes its default. Paths may start with ~/ for the home directory.

$schema.description: Editor hint pointing at this schema. Ignored by mexxi.

paths.description: Where mexxi lives and where it creates task worktrees.
paths.why: mexxi has to know where its own clone is and where to put each task's copy of a repository.

checkout.description: The mexxi clone the hosts are linked to. The installer refuses to run from any other clone.

worktreeRoot.description: Directory under which ibni creates a folder per repository, holding each task's worktree and its evidence directory.

hosts.description: Which coding-agent hosts the installer links the workflow into. Switching one off removes what an earlier install gave it: links, settings and hooks entries, and Claude Code mods.
hosts.why: You may use only one or two of the three agents, and mexxi should touch only those.

codex.description: Install for Codex (~/.codex or CODEX_HOME, plus ~/.agents/skills).

models.description: Model per role and host. null means the role inherits the host's own model.
models.why: Different jobs suit different models, and a reviewer from another model family catches what the builder's family misses.

crossFamilyReviewer.description: A reviewer model from a different family to the implementer's, as provider/model, because a reviewer from the builder's own family shares its blind spots. Rendered as the code-reviewer's model in place of reviewer. null falls back to the reviewer's model.

claude.description: Claude Code models, as an alias (opus, sonnet, haiku) or a full model ID.

crossFamilyReviewer.description: A Codex model that `ibni cross-review` runs the code-reviewer on through codex exec in a read-only sandbox, so the reviewer is not the implementer's family and does not share its blind spots. null, or Codex not installed, falls back to the reviewer's model and says so in the pull request's Evidence.
Codex has only one family, so this is simply used in place of reviewer as the code-reviewer's model; null falls back to the reviewer's model.

workflow.description: Defaults the workflow applies to every repository.
workflow.why: Branch names, screen sizes and free ports differ from one team and machine to the next.

branchPrefix.description: Prefix for task branches; a repository instruction may still ask for another with --prefix.

viewports.description: Viewport widths in CSS pixels that rendered QA covers: desktop, tablet and mobile.

ports.description: Range ibni assigns each new workspace's PORT from, so parallel worktrees' dev servers do not collide. Ports already recorded by a retained workspace or bound on this machine are skipped.

first.description: Lowest port ibni assigns. Each task gets its own port from this range, so two tasks can run their development servers at once.

last.description: Highest port ibni assigns; at least first.

review.description: How the independent code-reviewer selects what to review.
review.why: The reviewer needs a way to choose what to read, and you may not have ocr installed.

tool.description: ocr runs OpenCodeReview's delegation mode (the ocr CLI) to choose the files and rules, and the reviewer judges them; it needs ocr installed. none has the reviewer read the diff itself, read-only, with no extra tool to install.

browser.description: The Playwright MCP server every host uses for rendered QA.
browser.why: The browser check should behave the same on every agent and every run, so the browser tooling is pinned to one version.

executablePath.description: Browser executable Playwright drives, such as /usr/bin/chromium. null uses Playwright's own Chromium for both the MCP server (--browser=chromium) and the rendered-QA sweep; install it once with npx -y @playwright/mcp@<playwrightMcpVersion> install-browser chromium.

outputDir.description: Where Playwright may write screenshots and recordings; null means paths.worktreeRoot, so evidence directories are writable.

guard.description: What the shared guard hook blocks on every host.
guard.why: A stuck agent occasionally runs something destructive, so a hook backs up the rules by stopping the commands you list.

deny.description: Command prefixes refused on every host: publishing, merges, releases and force pushes by default. Add your own production deploys, such as firebase deploy, npm run deploy, gcloud run deploy, vercel --prod or netlify deploy --prod; setting the list replaces the default, so keep the default entries you want. The installer also writes each as a Bash(<prefix>:*) permissions.deny rule in Claude Code's settings.json; the guard hook repeats them as patterns, because a prefix rule is sidestepped by cd x && <command>.

protectedBranches.description: Branches the guard refuses to push to, in addition to each repository's default branch.

blockUnquotedGlobs.description: Refuse unquoted --include=* and --exclude=* globs, which zsh expands (and aborts on when nothing matches) unless setopt no_nomatch reaches the agent's shell. Leave off once a fresh Claude Code session shows `grep -rn x --include=*.ts .` searching; turn on if it fails with 'no matches found'.

repeatedFailureLimit.description: How many times the same shell command may fail in one agent session, with no file edited in between, before the loop breaker tells the agent to stop retrying and re-diagnose.

claude.description: Claude Code-only settings: the ones the installer merges into Claude Code's own settings.json (alongside the deny rules and hooks it owns; everything else in that file stays yours), and the ones the mods read.
claude.why: Claude Code has settings the other agents lack, such as its limit on how long a shell command may run.

bashMaxTimeoutMs.description: Longest a foreground Bash command may run (BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS), in milliseconds. Set it above your slowest repository's verify run; the default is 15 minutes.

contextNudgePercent.description: Context window fill, in percent, at which the run pane's band suggests a fresh session and ibni adopt for follow-ups.

forge.description: Which code forge a repository's pull requests, CI state, issues and media URLs come from: GitHub through gh, GitLab through glab. github.com and gitlab.com are known; a repository can name its own with "forge" in its committed .mexxi.json, which wins over this group. A remote on any other host has no forge, and the steps that need one fail or skip with the reason.
forge.why: mexxi has to know whether a repository lives on GitHub or GitLab to open its pull requests and read its CI.

hosts.description: Self-hosted forges by the host in the push remote's URL (with its port for an http(s) remote), as github or gitlab, such as {"git.example.com": "gitlab"}. An SSH host alias (git@github-work:owner/repo) needs no entry: ibni resolves it through ssh config, as gh does, and ssh.github.com counts as github.com.

jev.description: Jev triage through OpenRouter; the API key is read from OPENROUTER_API_KEY, never from this file.
jev.why: Jev is an outside decision model, reached through OpenRouter. This tests whether it would choose a task's checks better than the agent, while only recording its answers.

stage.description: What triage may do with its answers. Only shadow exists: it records answers beside the agent's own gate choices and changes nothing. Escalate (add a gate on a confident answer) and skip (drop the independent review on a confident mechanical answer) come only once shadow data shows agreement.

model.description: Pinned Jev model; not the ~typesafe/jev-latest alias, so a release cannot shift answers mid-calibration.

endpoint.description: OpenRouter's Decisions API, which takes the question schema triage sends. It receives the API key, so it must be HTTPS; plain HTTP is allowed only on loopback (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]), where a local stand-in never sends the key over a network.

owners.description: GitHub accounts and organisations that are yours. A listed repository owned by anyone else is skipped, since its content is not only yours to share. Jev runs only on github.com: a repository on GitLab or a self-hosted forge is skipped.

repositories.description: Repositories (owner/name, as in the push remote's github.com URL) triage may run in.

maxPayloadBytes.description: Each request stays below this many bytes; larger text puts Jev in a slower, less accurate long-context mode.

timeoutMs.description: How long one request may take before triage gives up and the run carries on.

zeroDataRetention.description: Ask OpenRouter to route only to providers that retain no data (provider.zdr). If none serves the model, calls fail and are recorded with the reason.

segwi.description: segwi, a local web app and MCP server for starting and following mexxi runs from your phone.
segwi.why: A run takes minutes to an hour and stops whenever it needs a reply or a permission, so without segwi you have to be at the terminal to keep it moving.

enabled.description: Install and run segwi at all.

bind.description: The address the server listens on.

host.description: Interface to listen on. Loopback only: the server refuses any other host, so reach it from other devices through tailscale serve.

runner.description: Which coding agent segwi starts. Only Claude Code exists so far.

model.description: Model every run uses, such as sonnet. Empty uses your coding agent's own default, which may cost more than a run needs.

allowUnsandboxed.description: Start runs even when Claude Code's sandbox can't start, because bubblewrap or socat is missing. Dangerous: without the sandbox, every command on the allow list, such as npm run or a test, runs with all of your access. It can write anywhere you can, reach any network address, and reach segwi itself to answer its own approvals.

repositories.description: The only repositories a run may start in, each with a name, the path of its control checkout and the actions allowed there (build, ready or ask).

name.description: Short name shown in the app.

actions.description: What a run may do here: build runs /wettaq, ready runs /lesti, ask answers a question without changing anything.

auth.description: Who may use the web app.

web.description: Sign-in for the web app. MCP clients always use a bearer token instead.

mode.description: localhost-only trusts anyone on this machine. tailscale-header trusts the identity header that tailscale serve sets, and only on loopback.

header.description: Request header that carries the signed-in identity in tailscale-header mode.

allowed.description: Identities allowed in tailscale-header mode. Empty means nobody.

hostname.description: This machine's name on your tailnet, such as my-machine.example.ts.net, as tailscale serve status shows it. In tailscale-header mode segwi answers only to it and to loopback names, so a web page on another site can't reach segwi by pointing its own name at this machine (DNS rebinding). Required in that mode.

limits.description: Caps that keep a run, or a runaway client, from costing more than you meant.

concurrentRuns.description: Runs that may work at the same time.

runsPerDay.description: Runs that may start in one day.

maxTurns.description: Agent turns one run may take before it stops.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes a run may sit without activity or a reply before segwi stops it.

hardTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes a run may last in total.

approvalTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes an approval waits for you before it counts as denied.

taskMaxChars.description: Longest task text a run accepts.

canary.description: The nightly check that your coding agent still works the way segwi expects.
canary.why: The agent's command line and output can change between versions, and a small real run each night finds that out before you do.

model.description: Model the canary run uses. A small one keeps the nightly cost to a few cents.

maxTurns.description: Agent turns the canary run may take before it stops.

push.description: Send a push notification when a run needs you, finishes or fails.

systemdUserUnit.description: Let the installer add systemd user units for the server and its nightly check. Linux only.

retro.description: Where session retrospectives go and how long transcripts are kept for them.
retro.why: Session transcripts are private, so retrospectives need a home that no public repository ever commits.

output.description: Where /irrifletti writes its reports. A relative path is inside the clone, where retro/ is gitignored; the command refuses a folder in a Git repository unless it is gitignored there with nothing tracked, so reports never reach a public repository.

transcriptRetentionDays.description: Days of host transcripts a retro reads.

mods.description: Which Claude Code mods the installer installs.
mods.why: Claude Code can load two optional extras: the run pane, which shows where a run stands beside the chat, and the command fixer, which repairs shell commands that would otherwise fail.
